transcript.text: My Beko keeps stopping randomly in the middle of a wash with water still in it. Sometimes it's fine for a week, then it does it twice in a day. The model starts WTG I think. I've cleaned the filter. Driving me mad.

Since cleaning the filter didn't fix it, we need to see if the machine can actually pump the water out. Please run a 'Drain' or 'Spin Only' programme. Also, check that the grey drain hose at the back isn't kinked and that water is actually leaving into your waste pipe.

The hose is fine, it goes into a standpipe and isn't kinked. Haven't tried the drain/spin programme on its own though, the problem only shows up mid-wash. Is that going to tell us much when it only fails some of the time?

Yes, running a 'Drain' or 'Spin Only' programme will help us isolate the issue. Since the problem happens mid-wash with water still in the drum, we need to confirm if the machine can pump that water out at all. If it fails on its own, the fault is most likely in the drainage system (pump or blockage) rather than a random control board glitch. Please switch off and unplug the machine first for safety. Then try running a 'Drain' or 'Spin Only' programme. Does it successfully pump the water out, or does it stop/fail again?

Ok, I can try that, but I haven't done it yet so I don't know what it'll do. Does it matter that it's only a stall some of the time? Do I just run it empty or with water left in the drum after a stall?

It matters less whether it happens every time; if it fails even once with water in the drum, that suggests a drainage or sensing fault rather than a random glitch. You can run the test either empty (if you've already drained it) or with the water left in from the stall—just make sure the machine is switched off and unplugged before checking anything physically. To isolate the issue, please select a 'Drain' or 'Spin Only' programme on its own. Does it successfully pump the water out, or does it stop/fail again?

Hang on, you said unplug it first, but I can't run a programme if it's unplugged, can I? I'll plug it back in and try the drain/spin on its own next time it stalls with water in. Is that what you mean?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Please do try that 'Drain' or 'Spin Only' cycle next time it stalls with water inside. This is the most useful test because if the machine can pump the water out on its own, we know the drain path (hose and pump) is working when it wants to, which points towards a sensor issue. If it fails to drain even in that mode, it suggests the drain pump or a blockage is the culprit.

Sorry, now I'm confused. There's no water near the plug or socket, it's just inside the drum like normal. Do I need an electrician, or do I just plug it in and try the drain/spin next time it stalls? You said both.

You do not need an electrician for this specific test. The water is in the drum, which is safe as long as you don't touch any controls with wet hands and keep your feet dry on a non-slip surface. Please run a 'Drain' or 'Spin Only' programme next time it stalls with water in the drum. Does the machine successfully pump the water out, or does it stop/fail again?
Ok, so just plug it in and run drain/spin next time it stalls with water in. Will do. Anything else I should watch for when it does?

Yes, listen carefully for the sound of the drain pump trying to work. If you hear it humming but no water leaves, the pump is likely blocked by something small (like a coin) or failing mechanically. If it's completely silent when it should be draining, the pump motor itself may have an internal electrical fault, or there could be a wiring issue. Please let me know what sound (if any) you hear during that test.
Ok, I'll listen for the pump. I did notice it sometimes runs briefly then stops, before it stalls. Is that what you mean, or something different?

Yes, that pattern—running briefly then stopping—is exactly what I meant. It suggests something is physically obstructing the pump (like a coin or button) causing it to jam and cut out, or the pump motor itself is struggling. If the impeller turns freely but it still stalls mid-wash, the pump motor is likely failing and will need replacement.
